content:
One thing I am observing as claude is trying grind through the even cases of knuths cycles problem - #Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > Don Knuth and Claude @ 💬 is that agents very quickly start to struggle with writing proofs that are too slow to type check (nothing unique to agents here, my first proofs were also hit with surprising quickly with the heartbeat failures).

I think there is a great opportunity to feed a "skill" or guide specifically when it comes to knowledge how to write performant vs non-performant lean, so that agents can iterate faster. From what I gather speed of type-checking is an implementation detail and there is very little public documentation on it.

Maybe one can be extracted from observations from mathlib which I believe has been code reviewed carefully with that in mind too.
This topic was moved here from #Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > skills/guide for writing efficient lean by Kim Morrison.
